clue.text: Plinth boy's broken a bit of a bloomer!

indicators.note: the boy has broken into the flower part, splitting it so his name sits inside

parts.note: a petal is one part of a flower, a bloomer
Des is a boy's name (short for Desmond); 's here means 'has'

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a lad snaps a piece off a flower on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a gaffe, but it is a flowering plant; 'boy's' reads as 'boy has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth is the base or stand that supports a statue, the same object as a pedestal.

clue.text: Witch is putting Gretel's head in pudding

indicators.note: the head letter is placed in the middle of the witch-plus-is string

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch
taken as written

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word Gretel

explanation.surface: The witch in Hansel and Gretel tries to cook the girl in a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: HAGGIS is a Scottish savoury pudding of offal and oatmeal cooked in a sheep's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is traditionally called a pudding in Scotland, a savoury boiled one.

clue.text: Profanity? There's a way to accommodate restriction on speech around University

indicators.note: one word is made to hold another inside it, as a host accommodates a guest

parts.note: a lane is a way or narrow road

indicators.note: the restriction is wrapped round the abbreviation for university

parts.note: a gag stops someone speaking

explanation.surface: A complaint about swearing and campus limits on free speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: 'mind your language' refers to swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad language means swearing, so the word alone can stand for profanity in that idiom.

clue.text: Left everything, not closing door

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is not included, so it is left without its close

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone walked out leaving everything, without shutting the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a grand doorway or gateway, so it is a kind of door.

clue.text: What's encountered lead etc. distributed next to hill?

definitions.text: What's encountered lead etc. distributed next to hill?

parts.note: met means encountered

indicators.note: the letters of the words are spread around into a new order

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A riddle about a gadget that has found scraps of lead and so on near a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges LEADETC into ALDETEC. The whole clue also describes the device, which has met buried metal on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal detector is the device that signals when it encounters buried metal objects like lead.

clue.text: Senior receiving support and guidance

indicators.note: the abbreviation takes in another piece, holding it between its letters

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: An older person getting help and advice.
explanation.walkthrough: STEER as a noun is informal for advice, as in 'a bum steer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a piece of advice or direction, a tip that guides someone.

clue.text: Pantomime character to dash round line, pursued by one of siblings

indicators.note: the sibling comes after, following behind like a chaser
the word for dash goes round the abbreviation for line

parts.note: to hare is to dash or run fast
a quin is one of five babies born together

explanation.surface: Stage directions for a pantomime chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the masked, chequered stock character of traditional pantomime and commedia.

clue.text: Nationalist, blocking theatre venues, stops progress

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits inside the venues word, blocking it in the middle

parts.note: stages are where plays are performed

explanation.surface: A political activist obstructs theatres and halts development.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stagnates ceases to develop or move forward, like still water.

clue.text: TV recording contest, catching end of second round

indicators.note: the verb for contest holds a letter, catching it inside

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word second

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A televised competition with a second round.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recording of moving pictures, as of a television programme.

clue.text: Time to encourage half-hearted floating voter — there's something valuable here

indicators.note: the double S at the heart of the word loses one, halving its middle

parts.note: to reassure is to encourage or hearten

indicators.note: floating suggests drifting and unsettled, so the letters move

explanation.surface: An election appeal to an undecided voter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two middle S's from REASSURE; 'floating' rearranges VOTER into TROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure trove is a hoard of valuables found hidden, so it is where something valuable lies.

clue.text: Author supporting our group with time

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
us is the speaker's group

explanation.surface: An author backed by a group, given time.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was a French novelist, the author of In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: Sweet cocktail of gin and rum with double the energy

indicators.note: a cocktail mixes ingredients, so the letters are mixed
the letter is taken twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sugary drink of gin and rum with an extra kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double the' gives EE, which is shuffled with GIN and RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A meringue is a dessert of baked whisked egg white and sugar, a confection or sweet.

clue.text: One Democrat interrupting Carol, being partial

indicators.note: the pieces break into the middle of the song word

parts.note: to carol is to sing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A politician cuts into a carol, showing bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Siding with someone means taking their part, so it is being partial or biased.

clue.text: Provided covering note and illumination on plane

indicators.note: the conditional word wraps round, covering the note

parts.note: if means provided that
light means illumination

explanation.surface: A deal including a banknote and lighting for an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: In-flight describes what happens aboard an aircraft during a journey, such as meals or films.

clue.text: Short-term view not good, as seen in finished rewritten document

indicators.note: the trimmed view appears inside the word for finished

parts.note: past means over, finished

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good is dropped

parts.note: a glimpse is a brief look

explanation.surface: A complaint about short-sightedness in a revised report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' removes G from GLIMPSE, leaving LIMPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript whose original writing has been erased and written over.

clue.text: Noise and speed in film

definitions.meaning: a loud continuous racket or clamour
the German standards scale once used to rate the sensitivity of photographic film

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a loud racket and also names a German standard for rating photographic film speed.

clue.text: Conservative mostly set about Liberal over wretched conditions

indicators.note: the trimmed word is placed about the other pieces, enclosing them
mostly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A Tory attacks a Liberal about poor living conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SQUARE to SQUAR. An over in cricket is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalor means filthy, miserable living conditions caused by neglect or poverty.

clue.text: Dispute possibly arising from rough estates?

indicators.note: the answer could come out of these letters once they are reordered

explanation.surface: Arguments that might break out on tough housing estates.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue the toss is an idiom meaning to dispute a decision that is already settled.

clue.text: Supporter with a flagstaff crossing street

indicators.note: the pole goes across the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a flagstaff is a pole

explanation.surface: A fan carrying a flag across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a vigorous advocate or champion of a cause, so a supporter.

clue.text: Finally do travel on a wide scale with first half of tour

parts.note: to get around is to travel widely

indicators.note: the first two of the four letters of the word tour are used

explanation.surface: Someone finally sets off on a world tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To get round to something means to do it at last after delay.

clue.text: One very diverted from work on crossword

indicators.note: the letter is turned away and taken out of the word

parts.note: to solve is to work out a puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone extremely distracted from a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means only or single, the one and only.

clue.text: Uncommonly generous: our new medical specialist

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remarkably generous new doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosurgeon is a doctor specialising in operations on the brain and nervous system.

clue.text: Band in these clues most fashionable of all?

definitions.meaning: the final clue of this puzzle ends with the word band, so band is its closing word
the latest thing, the very height of fashion

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the final word in a sequence and, idiomatically, the very latest fashion.

clue.text: Senior officer present in pub before end of night, speaking unclearly

indicators.note: the pub with its contents comes before the final letter
the officer and the present word go inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
CO is commanding officer
here means present

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word night

explanation.surface: A commanding officer drinking in a pub late at night slurs his words.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoherent speech is muddled and unclear, hard to follow.

clue.text: Two notes encapsulating one other composer

indicators.note: the pair of letters encloses the other pieces like a capsule
two means the letter is taken twice

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note
I is the Roman numeral one
else means other

explanation.surface: Two musical notes wrapped around another composer's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer of symphonies, so he fits a generic composer.

clue.text: Criticism chamber group finally discounted, investing in historic instrument

indicators.note: the shortened group is put into the instrument, clothing it inside

parts.note: a viol is an early bowed string instrument

indicators.note: the last letter of the group word is left out

parts.note: a trio is a three-player chamber ensemble

explanation.surface: Harsh words for a chamber group that put its money into an old instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is savage, caustic criticism, from the corrosive acid.

clue.text: Work some ideas up once, reflecting

indicators.note: reflecting means the letters are mirrored, read the other way
some means only a part of the words is used

explanation.surface: An old piece of writing mirrors some ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, often numbered in a composer's catalogue.

clue.text: Curtailment of musical performance by band

indicators.note: the tail, its final letter, is cut off the word

parts.note: Gigi is a famous film musical by Lerner and Loewe

explanation.surface: A band's concert cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' looks like an adjective for the performance, but it is a noun: the musical GIGI.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a single live performance by musicians, especially a band.
